title: Cyrus and the Bakery
premise: Ivo Halloran, a wedding planner who stopped believing in love after her own engagement collapsed, has spent three years living quietly above a failing bakery, writing anonymous letters to a stranger in prison—a pen-pal program she joined to feel useful without being seen. When Cyrus Ashford is released and moves into the flat next door, neither recognizes the other at first, but the truth surfaces slowly through shared bread, small kindnesses, and the bakery's fight against a predatory developer. As the neighborhood festival becomes their last chance to save the bakery, Ivo must choose between her carefully invisible life and a man who knows her deepest self only as a signatureless voice—and she must let him stay past the last train, past the festival, past every safe exit she has built. The story ends with the bakery saved, Cyrus choosing to stay not out of debt or gratitude but love, and Ivo signing her name to her letters for the first time.
about_author: R. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former small-town baker turned novelist who writes romances about people rebuilding themselves in kitchens, courtrooms, and quiet streets. They live somewhere coastal with a sourdough starter older than most of their friendships.

chapters.title: The Weight of White Sugar
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She plans a flawless wedding for clients she envies, then returns home to the crumbling bakery below her flat, where the elderly owner, Marguerite, gives her day-old loaves and unsolicited wisdom. Establishes Ivo's numbness and her ritual of writing an anonymous letter she never signs. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Ivo's POV: three years ago, her engagement ended publicly and humiliatingly; she joined a prison pen-pal program to pour her grief into someone who couldn't see her face. We meet the voice of 'C' on paper—wry, honest, hungry for news of ordinary life. Emotional beat: the birth of intimacy without identity.

chapters.title: Moving Day
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Released after ten years, he takes a cheap flat next to a bakery because the parole officer suggested routine. He carries one possession that matters: a shoebox of letters from someone called only 'V.' He doesn't know what she looks like and half hopes never to find out. Emotional beat: terror of freedom.

chapters.title: Flour on the Stairs
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A stranger helps carry her groceries up the stairs during a rainstorm; flour dusts his sleeves and he flinches when she thanks him too warmly. Neither catches the other's name. That night she writes to C about 'a neighbor with prison eyes,' not knowing why she's sure. Emotional beat: recognition without knowing.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A development firm offers to buy the bakery building; Marguerite refuses, but her hands shake afterward. Ivo finds the offer letter and feels an old anger stir—the same fury she buried with her engagement. First hint she'll fight for something again. Emotional beat: dormant courage waking.

chapters.title: Bread at Midnight
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Unable to sleep, he smells bread baking at 2 a.m. and finds Marguerite teaching Ivo to knead, badly. He's invited in before he can refuse. The warmth terrifies him; kindness was currency in prison, always a debt. Emotional beat: learning to accept a gift.

chapters.title: What the Letters Never Said
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Cyrus rereads V's letters, noticing how she dodged every personal detail. Ivo writes about her fear that C will be released someday and hate her for the things she withheld. Dramatic irony tightens: they describe each other to each other. Emotional beat: the gap between honesty and disclosure.

chapters.title: A Wedding Refused
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A lucrative client asks her to plan a wedding identical to her own ruined one. She declines, jeopardizing her business, and can't explain why even to herself. Cyrus witnesses her walking out and recognizes the look—he wore it at his own trial. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Parole and Paperwork
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. His parole officer warns him against attachments; employers reject him twice in one afternoon. Marguerite hires him to fix the bakery's ancient oven, paying cash and asking no questions. He almost cries over a wrench. Emotional beat: dignity restored by small work.

chapters.title: The Festival Committee
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The neighborhood festival needs an organizer; Marguerite volunteers Ivo before she can refuse. Planning a festival feels dangerously like planning a wedding—but this one is hers to shape. Cyrus offers to help with logistics, and she accepts before thinking. Emotional beat: stepping back into the world.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over oven repairs, Cyrus tells Ivo fragments of his crime—arson, a fire meant for a slumlord that spread further than intended. Ivo tells him nothing true about herself. She goes home ashamed and writes C the confession she couldn't speak aloud. Emotional beat: asymmetry of trust.

chapters.title: The Slumlord's Name
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The developer pressuring Marguerite is the nephew of the man Cyrus burned for—the same family, the same methods. His old rage ignites, and he must decide whether justice outside the law ever actually worked. He chooses the bakery instead, sanding floors until his hands bleed. Emotional beat: rage redirected into repair.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. After the festival's first success—a fundraiser bake sale—Ivo and Cyrus nearly kiss in the empty kitchen. She pulls away, terrified of being known. He apologizes for misreading and leaves. That night she realizes she wanted to be misread. Emotional beat: desire versus safety.

chapters.title: The Shoebox Question
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He asks Ivo casually whether she's ever written to strangers; she lies fluently and hates herself for it. Meanwhile he drafts a letter to V announcing his release, unable to send it—afraid she'll stop writing once he's free and real. Emotional beat: cowardice on both sides of the wall.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. City inspectors, tipped off anonymously, condemn the bakery's ovens days before the festival. Marguerite suspects the developer. Ivo recognizes sabotage and, for the first time in three years, gets angry in public. Emotional beat: protective fury.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Oven
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He knows masonry from prison maintenance and leads the rebuild, teaching Ivo, Marguerite, and neighborhood kids brick by brick. Working side by side, Ivo laughs for the first time in the book. Cyrus falls for the sound completely. Emotional beat: joy as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Letter He Sent
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Drunk on hope after the rebuild, Cyrus finally mails his letter to V, telling her where he lives and asking her to come. Then panic: what if she's disappointed? What if she was never real? He watches the mailbox like a wound. Emotional beat: vulnerability mailed and irrevocable.

chapters.title: Return to Sender
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The letter arrives. Ivo reads it eleven times, writes three replies, burns them all. She starts avoiding Cyrus, inventing festival errands. Marguerite notices and says nothing, but leaves extra bread at Ivo's door like a rebuke. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into avoidance.

chapters.title: The Eviction Notice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The developer escalates: code violations, a court date set for the week after the festival. Ivo realizes the festival isn't just celebration—it's evidence the bakery matters. She throws herself into organizing with a planner's ruthlessness that surprises everyone, including her. Emotional beat: purpose replacing fear.

chapters.title: Cyrus's Past Arrives
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A tabloid runs his photo—'ARSONIST NEXT DOOR'—and neighbors waver. Some shopkeepers pull out of the festival. Marguerite defends him publicly, and Ivo, watching, feels her silence become its own betrayal. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by distance.

chapters.title: What V Withheld
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, confessional. Alone, Ivo admits why she never told C everything: her fiancé left her at the altar, and she'd testified—hesitantly, uselessly—as a character witness in a case that helped convict a man like Cyrus. Her letters were penance. She fears C will see her as part of the machine that caged him. Emotional beat: shame's false logic.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Cyrus confronts Ivo about her avoidance; she deflects cruelly, implying ex-cons shouldn't get comfortable. He leaves. Both narrate the same scene with different wounds visible. Marguerite overhears and, for the first time, is angry at Ivo. Emotional beat: cruelty as self-protection.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Story
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She reveals her own history: a husband lost to a wrongful conviction, a life spent feeding people because courts failed her. She tells Ivo plainly: 'You write to him because judging is easy at a distance. Love isn't.' Ivo realizes Marguerite may have guessed long ago. Emotional beat: inherited wisdom.

chapters.title: The Draft
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo writes the letter she should have written years ago—her full name, her full history, her testimony, her cowardice—and seals it without reading it twice. She doesn't mail it yet. It sits on her table like a lit fuse. Emotional beat: truth prepared but not delivered.

chapters.title: Festival Eve
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV shifts. Final preparations: stalls built, ovens tested, the whole street strung with lights. Cyrus and Ivo work late, civil and aching. He tells her he wrote to someone once, someone who kept him sane, and that he's waiting for her answer. Ivo's blood runs cold. Emotional beat: the walls thinning.

chapters.title: The Festival
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The festival blooms—bread, music, testimony from neighbors about what the bakery means. The developer's lawyer lurks, photographing violations. Attendance becomes legal argument. Ivo orchestrates it flawlessly while searching the crowd for courage. Emotional beat: community as armor.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. V's reply arrives mid-festival: not forgiveness, not a name—just 'I'm sorry. I'm not who you think.' Cyrus understands she's close, maybe watching. Devastated, he decides to leave town on the last train rather than haunt a woman who regrets him. Emotional beat: heartbreak mistaken for mercy.

chapters.title: Platform Nine
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo learns from Marguerite that Cyrus bought a ticket. She runs—through the festival, past the stalls—to the station, carrying the sealed letter. The train waits. She must decide in ninety seconds whether to let him go or let him stay. Emotional beat: the blurb's promise arriving.

chapters.title: Stay
chapters.summary: Dual POV. On the platform, Ivo says only: 'Don't take the last train. Please.' She hands him the unsealed letter and walks away before he reads it. He reads her name, her testimony, her shame—and boards anyway, then steps off as doors close, choosing her over the mystery. Emotional beat: surrender on both sides.

chapters.title: After the Doors Close
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He finds Ivo on the empty platform and they say the plain truths: he isn't angry about her testimony; she isn't the villain of his story; the letters were the realest thing either of them had. No kiss yet—just sitting together as the tracks go quiet. Emotional beat: relief after rupture.

chapters.title: Court
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The bakery's hearing arrives. Ivo testifies—not hesitantly this time—about what the bakery means, marshaling festival photos, petitions, and Marguerite's forty-year lease. Cyrus watches her use the skills her old life gave her for something worth winning. Emotional beat: justice inside the law, finally.

chapters.title: The Verdict and the Fire
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The developer, losing legally, retaliates: a small fire in the bakery's storage room. No one is hurt, but Cyrus stands in the smoke shaking—fire was his sin, and now it's aimed at the people he loves. Old shame threatens to swallow the new man. Emotional beat: the past weaponized.

chapters.title: Suspect
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Police question Cyrus first—it's obvious and unjust. Ivo provides his alibi without hesitation, publicly, in front of neighbors who doubted him. The gesture costs her some clients and gains her something better. Emotional beat: belief as action, not feeling.

chapters.title: The Real Arsonist
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus and a retired firefighter neighbor trace the fire to the developer's contractor. Instead of revenge, Cyrus gathers evidence and hands it to the journalist who once smeared him—justice by daylight, the way he couldn't have managed at twenty-three. Emotional beat: becoming the man the letters believed in.

chapters.title: Sign Here
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The developer withdraws; the building is protected by a community land trust Ivo organized. Marguerite makes Ivo co-owner of the bakery. Ivo, who planned other people's weddings for a living, is handed keys to her own future and doesn't know how to hold them. Emotional beat: receiving what you didn't dare want.

chapters.title: First Names
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Quiet domestic chapter: Cyrus bakes (badly), Ivo teaches him cake decorating, they argue about frosting like people with a future. They tell each other the small biographies the letters skipped—favorite colors, worst birthdays. Intimacy rebuilt from details. Emotional beat: ordinary love arriving.

chapters.title: The Wedding She Plans
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo takes one wedding client again—Marguerite's granddaughter—and plans it with joy instead of dread. Cyrus helps. Standing in the crowd at the reception, Ivo realizes she believes in weddings again, or at least in what they can hold. Emotional beat: faith restored by witness.

chapters.title: The Question
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus asks Ivo, not for marriage but for permanence: renew his lease, share hers, build something. She panics briefly—old reflex—then remembers the platform, the closed doors, the choice already made. She says yes before he finishes. Emotional beat: fear answered with yes.

chapters.title: Signed, Ivo
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo writes one final letter to C—full circle—and delivers it by hand across the hall, signed with her name for the first time. It says everything the earlier letters couldn't: thank you, I'm sorry, I'm here. Emotional beat: the anonymous self retired.

chapters.title: Bakery Hours
chapters.summary: Ensemble epilogue. One year later: the bakery thrives, Marguerite holds court, the festival is annual, and Cyrus teaches a baking class for newly released men. Ivo locks up at closing, flips the sign, and lets him stay—no trains, no exits, no signature needed. Emotional beat: home, chosen daily.
